thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Incident page fired for routing-controller-service in us-west-2 — 5xx spike and elevated latency for hosted inference (autopage rule: routing-controller-5xx-threshold). PagerDuty: page to oncall-mike.

mike: acked. taking this — moving to #incident-bridge. Can someone grab runbooks? :headphones:

sara: on it. starting with routing-controller health checks + autoscaler status. sharing quick checks: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=routing-controller -o wide` and `kubectl -n inference describe hpa routing-controller`.

juan: seeing heavy backlog on the request-queue metric (approx 3x usual). Also some connection churn to the upstream model pool. Could be a cascade from a recent model rollout.

mike: noted. sara, run the health checks and report pod restarts / OOMs. juan, can you check if recent rollout rotated any model variants in the last 30m? `deployments.apps/routing-controller` revision history.

sara: health checks: 2 pods in CrashLoopBackOff earlier, restarted by k8s 2x. logs show repeated `TimeoutError: upstream read timeout` from model-proxy. paste log snippet:```\n2025-11-14T21:20:13Z routing-controller error upstream read timeout id=abcd1234\n2025-11-14T21:20:14Z routing-controller warn queue length=512\n```

juan: rollout history shows a canary for model-embed-v2 deployed ~25m ago. Canary traffic fraction 20%. Could be overload on the new variant's node pool.

mike: okay plan: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% (rollback to stable routing), 2) scale routing-controller to +2 pods, 3) enable fallback routing to model-embed-v1 for affected routes. Sara/juan, execute steps and call out any failures. I'll keep PD ownership and update stakeholders.

sara: scaling routing-controller now: `kubectl scale deployment routing-controller --replicas=6 -n inference` — started, pods spinning up.

juan: setting canary traffic to 0 via traffic-split service patch, applying now. patch command: `kubectl apply -f /ops/traffic-split/canary-zero.yml` — applied.

sara: routing-controller scaled, new pods ready. verifying metrics: queue depth decreasing from 512 -> 120 over 3 minutes.

mike: :thumbsup: good progress. Any customer-facing impact?

juan: partial — some small customers using the canary got 503s. Enterprise dedicated clusters unaffected. I put a short status note in the status page: "Intermittent 5xx errors for hosted inference in us-west-2; mitigation in progress."

mike: calling the incident severity: sev2 for now given partial customer impact. Assigning primary to eng-runtime (alex) for follow-up root cause & postmortem. I'll stay on until handoff.

alex: ack. I'll take primary after initial mitigation. Please confirm when routing stabilizes and canary is fully disabled.

sara: confirmed: canary traffic now 0%, fallback routes to v1 are active. 5xx rate near baseline, latency returned to normal.

mike: I'm handing ownership to alex at 21:32 UTC — continuing monitoring for 30m then run a post-incident triage. alex, want me to leave the bridge or transfer the channel?

alex: please leave the bridge after you drop the PD ownership. I'll keep the bridge open for the triage. Thanks for quick mitigation.

mike: dropping PD ownership now — `pagerduty:ack clear` (actioned). If anything flares, re-escalate. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

pagerbot: PagerDuty: owner cleared for incident routing-controller-service (incident# 3251).

alex: capturing notes: mitigation steps executed (scale +2, canary -> 0%, fallback to v1). Initial suspected cause: canary model variant overloaded its node pool causing upstream timeouts; cascading queue buildup at routing-controller. Postmortem owner: alex (eng-runtime). I'll open a postmortem ticket and link runbook fixes: - harder throttling on canary, - better autoscaler tuning, - add quicker automated rollback on request-queue threshold.

sara: quick follow-ups: I'll add a dashboard panel for model-canary queue delta and an alert that triggers before queue exceeds 400.

juan: I'll look into model-pool capacity and the canary node pool size; propose autoscaling changes or moving canary to less-loaded nodes during rollout.

alex: thanks all. final status update to customers scheduled in 30m once we confirm stability. Closing this slack thread after triage notes posted. :white_check_mark:
